translationRepairs: Working with Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Xiao Dexiu, he revised the statutes. The emperor addressed Shucheng: "At present the penalties in our statutes are inconsistent in severity.

Working with Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Xiao De, he revised the statutes. The emperor addressed Shucheng: "At present the penalties in our statutes are inconsistent in severity.
與樞密副使蕭德修定法令 is Xiao De (蕭德) plus 修定 “revise the statutes,” not a name Xiao Dexiu; s0016’s 從宜修定 confirms 修定 as the verb.

With Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Xiao Dexiu he revised the statutes. The emperor issued an edict to Shucheng saying: "At present the statutes' severity and leniency are not in proper order.

With Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Xiao De he revised the statutes. The emperor issued an edict to Shucheng saying: "At present the statutes' severity and leniency are not in proper order.
Same parse: 蕭德 is the personal name and 修定法令 the action; the literal must not glue 修 into the name Xiao Dexiu.

Early in Xianyong his fief was transferred to Qi. Summoned to court, he received the title Meritous Minister of Shared Virtue, was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with concurrent appointment as Central Secretariat Director, and was appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. His fief was then changed to Jin, he was granted the attendants allotted to both the chancellor's and the commissioner's offices, and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

Early in Xianyong his fief was transferred to Qi. Summoned to court, he received the title Meritorious Minister of Shared Virtue, was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with concurrent appointment as Central Secretariat Director, and was appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. His fief was then changed to Jin, he was granted the attendants allotted to both the chancellor's and the commissioner's offices, and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
同德功臣 is a meritorious-minister honor; English “Meritous” is a misspelling of “Meritorious,” and the rest of the sentence matches 咸雍初…封趙王.

At the beginning of Xianyong his fief was changed to Qi; he was summoned and granted the title Meritous Minister of Shared Virtue, made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Central Secretariat Director, appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, had his fief changed to Jin, was given attendants of both the chancellor's and the commissioner's offices, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

Same typo fix for 同德功臣: “Meritorious” is the correct English spelling in the literal field.
